newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian region, Duferco agree Clabecq restart.
newsitem.headline: Belgian region, Duferco agree Clabecq restart.

text.p: The Belgian Walloon region and Italian-Swiss firm Duferco have reached an agreement for a partial takeover of bankrupt Belgian steel firm Clabecq, they said on Saturday, following a late-night agreement Friday.
"We have an agreement with Duferco, so that we can restart the company early next year," Pierrre Sonveaux, chef de cabinet of Walloon minister-president Robert Collignon, told Belgian television RTL.
The deal is conditional on approval by Clabecq workers, who must vote on it before July 15.
"It is up to the workers to decide now," Duferco director Roberto Grosso said.
Under the agreement, 820 of Clabecq's 1800 workers will get a job in the new firm, albeit at less favourable conditions.
"Wages were too high at Clabecq, there will have to be talks about new wage conditions," said Alain Zenner, one of Clabecq's court-appointed receivers.
The new company will have a 1.4 billion franc capital, of which 1.05 billion will be contributed by Duferco and 350 million by SWS, the investment holding company of the Walloon region.
Duferco, a private steel and commodities trader, announced in April it was studying a possible takeover of Clabecq.
Receivers have been trying to find a buyer for Clabecq since the company was declared bankrupt in January.
Clabecq is majority-owned by the Walloon Region.
